ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — History and Physical — Jim Thorpe

code.originalText: New patient with a non-healing sore on the lower lip and chest tightness on exertion: lip biopsy, coronary disease assessment, secondary prevention, and care preferences

text.paragraph: New patient with a non-healing sore on the lower lip and chest tightness on exertion: lip biopsy, coronary disease assessment, secondary prevention, and care preferences [S]
This fictional modern episode addresses the presenting concerns below. [S]

list.item: A sore on his lower lip has not healed for three months, and he wants to know whether it is cancer. [S]
He gets tight in the chest walking uphill and wants to stay active enough to keep coaching. [S]
He wants his care to respect who he is and to be told plainly about costs and choices. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: James Francis Thorpe was born a twin on the Sac and Fox reservation near present Prague, Oklahoma, to Hiram and Charlotte Vieux Thorpe. His Sac and Fox name, Wa-tho-huck, means "Bright Path." He is usually considered Sac and Fox and was brought up as a member of the Sac and Fox tribe; he also had Potawatomi, Kickapoo, Menominee, Irish and French ancestry. The Oklahoma Historical Society gives his birth as May 28, 1888, noting that his estate cites 1887; another reference work gives May 22, 1887. [D]
His twin brother, Charles, died of pneumonia just short of their eighth birthday; his mother died when he was twelve and his father when he was sixteen. [D]

He attended federal boarding schools, including the Sac and Fox Indian Agency School, Haskell Institute, and from 1903 the Carlisle Indian School in Pennsylvania, where he became a track and football star. [D]

At the 1912 Olympic Games in Stockholm he won gold medals in the pentathlon and decathlon. In January 1913 the Amateur Athletic Union stripped him of his medals because he had played semiprofessional baseball; in 1982 the International Olympic Committee recognized him as co-winner, and on July 15, 2022 it restored him as sole winner of both events. [D]

He played major-league baseball from 1913 to 1919 and professional football into 1928, and was the first president of the American Professional Football Association, the forerunner of the National Football League. Afterwards he worked as a film extra and in construction, as a security guard and ditch digger, at the Ford plant in Dearborn during the Second World War, and in the Merchant Marine in 1945; he became a critic of the Bureau of Indian Affairs, lectured widely, and worked to inspire American Indians. [D]

He reportedly had an alcohol problem; one reference work states that excessive drinking began at Carlisle and troubled him for the rest of his life and frustrated his attempts at a stable married life. [D]
In 1951 he was treated for lip cancer as a charity patient in a Philadelphia hospital, where he had an operation. [D]
He had a heart attack in 1943. [D]
In 1950 an Associated Press poll named him the greatest athlete of the first half of the twentieth century. [D]

list.item: Former Olympic champion and professional football and baseball player. Since then has worked in construction, security work and film work, served in the merchant marine, and now speaks at schools and community events and coaches young athletes [S]
Sun exposure: decades of outdoor training, play and construction work, rarely with a hat or lip protection; two blistering sunburns of the lips that he remembers [S]
Tobacco: smoked about a pack of cigarettes a day from his twenties until his heart attack eight years ago (about 35 pack-years); no smokeless tobacco since [S]
Alcohol: drank heavily in earlier years and cut down on his own after his heart attack; now one or two beers on some weekends (AUDIT-C 2) [S]

Enrolled member of the Sac and Fox Nation; lives with his wife in a small house he rents; has health insurance through a public program. Asked how he would like his care organized, he said he wanted his care here and would like information about Sac and Fox Nation and Indian Health Service health programs before deciding whether to use them [S]

Strengths and supports: lifelong athlete who still walks and throws a ball with the young people he coaches; speaks about education and opportunity for Native youth; proud of his family and community [S]

Suspicious for squamous cell carcinoma; incisional biopsy taken today and otolaryngology consultation booked

Suspicious for squamous cell carcinoma; incisional biopsy taken today and otolaryngology consultation booked: active, confirmed [S]

Chronic coronary disease with stable exertional angina: tightness in the chest when walking uphill or carrying loads for about a year, relieved by two or three minutes of rest, never at rest; heart attack eight years ago, treated in hospital, with no regular care or medicines since. Resting ECG: sinus rhythm with Q waves in the inferior leads. Synthetic modern episode linked to his documented heart attacks: active, confirmed [S]

Incisional biopsy of the lip lesion today, with pathology; sun protection for the lips and skin (lip balm with SPF 30 or higher, a broad-brimmed hat); dental review. Guideline: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Head and Neck Cancers (cancer of the lip and oral cavity) (2026); Skin Cancer Prevention: Behavioral Counseling (2018) [S]

Otolaryngology (head and neck surgery) consultation for a suspected lip cancer: staging, treatment, management of the neck, and surveillance. Guideline: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Head and Neck Cancers (cancer of the lip and oral cavity) (2026) [S]

Secondary prevention for chronic coronary disease: aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 80 mg with a lipid panel 4 to 12 weeks after starting and a goal LDL below 55 mg/dL, metoprolol succinate for angina, sublingual nitroglycerin with written instructions, blood pressure below 130/80, an echocardiogram to measure heart function before surgery, and staying tobacco-free. Guideline: 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); 2018 AHA/ACC/AACVPR/AAPA/ABC/ACPM/ADA/AGS/APhA/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline on the Management of Blood Cholesterol (2018); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, ischemic heart disease monograph (2026) [S]

Cardiac rehabilitation once the lip wound has healed: up to 36 supervised exercise and education sessions for stable angina, with nutrition, activity, and risk-factor coaching. Guideline: 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, ischemic heart disease monograph (2026) [S]

Care organized around his choices: information about Sac and Fox Nation health services and Indian Health Service, tribal, and urban Indian health programs, help to use them if he wishes, and room for any traditional or spiritual practices he chooses; costs and options explained plainly. Guideline: Purchased/Referred Care (2026) [S]
Referral to otolaryngology (head and neck surgery), Lucia Ferrante, MD, ordered 2026-06-08 [S]
